body:
Dense Calendar release probes retain the current renderer. Initial-header removal and layout/paint containment did not establish useful stable readiness gains. Automatic content visibility repeated an 8-15 ms local and 74-77 ms constrained warm gain at 1000 cards, but a controlled large-text probe exposed underestimated skipped heights. The remembered-size variant also failed this geometry check; all prototypes were restored.

A separate registered release Engine fixture with 100 projects, 10k cards, 1000 milestones and 50k note reports measures the existing global Calendar page at 14.25 ms median / 14.69 ms p95 and a scoped page at 0.77 / 0.79 ms (200 samples after 20 warm calls). Early type filtering gives no gain: SQLite already uses the card and milestone branch indexes. Ordered items, source versions, event fields, pagination, freshness and warnings remain equivalent.

The full gate passes 269 Rust, 139 JavaScript and 12 Python tests. Relevant release Chromium/WebKit Calendar interactions pass, with inspected Chromium screenshots. The deployed application implementation is unchanged; no manual restart is needed. Broader widget work, transport, concurrency, physical devices and full release acceptance remain open. Evidence: progress/2026-10-01-calendar-probes.md.

metadata.summary: Calendar audit rejects unsafe height skipping and ineffective geometry/query shortcuts.
